3	description: Export the current Claude Code session to the local Context Explorer container — transcript, subagent files, and an as-transcribed snapshot of the in-context system prompt and tool definitions. Use when the user runs /context-export or asks to export/inspect this session's context.

7

9

13	summarized.

17	```bash
18	curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:7331/api/health
19	```
20	
21	If this fails, tell the user to start it (`docker compose up -d` in
22	`~/ContextExplorer`) and stop here.
23	
24	## Step 2 — locate the session
25	
26	- **Session ID**: your system prompt's scratchpad directory path contains it:
27	  `.../<project-slug>/<SESSION-ID>/scratchpad`. If no scratchpad path is present,
28	  fall back to the newest-mtime `*.jsonl` in the project dir below.
29	- **Project slug**: the current working directory with `/` and `.` replaced by `-`
30	  (e.g. `/Users/x/proj` → `-Users-x-proj`).
31	- **Transcript**: `~/.claude/projects/<project-slug>/<SESSION-ID>.jsonl` — verify it
32	  exists and is non-empty before continuing.
33	
34	## Step 3 — upload transcript and companion files

43

47	    "http://127.0.0.1:7331/api/import/file?session=<id>&name=$(python3 - "$f" <<'EOF'
48	import sys, urllib.parse; print(urllib.parse.quote(sys.argv[1][2:], safe=''))
49	EOF
50	)"
51	done
52	```
53	
54	## Step 4 — transcribe your in-context material (the critical step)
55	
56	Create a staging directory in your scratchpad: `ctx-export/` with subdirs
57	`system-prompt/` and `tools/`.
58

content.text:
The cross-session export cache is built, tested end-to-end, and the mid-turn readout request is in too.

**The shared library — how the "statically defined shit" stops being re-exported:**

- **Content-addressed store on the server** (`/data/library/`): every system-prompt section and tool definition is keyed `name@sha256-prefix`. It **seeds itself automatically** — at boot from all stored snapshots (13 unique sections + 16 tools appeared immediately, duplicates collapsing by hash), and on every future snapshot import. No separate maintenance step.
- **Exports send references, not text.** `/context-export` now starts step 4 with `GET /api/library/manifest`, which returns per-entry **fingerprints**: head/middle/tail excerpts plus length for sections, and description fingerprint + sorted schema parameter names for tools. The model compares those excerpts against what's actually in its context — the one step that can't be mechanized, since only the model sees the context, but *comparing* three excerpts is ~100× cheaper than *transcribing* 40k tokens. Matches become tiny `.ref` files; the server re-inflates them at import with `provenance: "library"` stamped on each entry, so the snapshot on disk stays fully self-contained and the viewer needs no changes. A repeat export should drop from ~40k model-output tokens to ~2k (the genuinely session-specific sections — environment, background-session, memory — are listed in the skill as always-transcribe-fresh, since they embed session ids and dates).
- **Verified round-trip:** built a staging dir with 2 section refs + 2 tool refs + 1 fresh section, ran `assemble.py` (which now reports "4 served from the shared library cache"), and confirmed the stored snapshot contains the full re-inflated text — the 19,286-character Workflow description included — with correct provenance markers. Mismatched or missing entries fall back to full transcription, which then seeds the cache for next time, so drift (a new CLI version changing a tool description) is self-healing rather than silently wrong.

**Window load surfaced globally** (your screenshot request): the tape header readout now always shows the full breakdown — `rec 1774/2339 · 120,539 tok in window (read 120,070 · write 468 · in 1 · out 279) · timestamp` — updating with every selection, on every tab, not just inside the System context pane.

Test snapshot cleaned up, skill re-synced to `~/.claude/skills/`, regression suite green, and the operational memory updated so future sessions know the library exists and how the skill should use it.

content.text: Classic CodeMirror 5 gotcha — its `.CodeMirror-scroll` element is *always* `overflow: scroll` internally (it hides the scrollbars with a negative-margin trick), so even a fully-expanded block eats wheel events over its whole area. The fix is the standard CM auto-resize recipe: kill the internal scroller for in-flow preview blocks so the wheel chains to the pane, while the intentionally-scrolling raw-mode viewers keep their own scroll.

content.text:
The mirror is live and already did its first sweep: **2,372 backup files across 104 sessions (45MB) copied into the container volume at boot**, with a re-sweep every 60 seconds.

How it works:

- **Copy-once polling, not fs-watching.** Backup files are immutable once written (`pathhash@vN`), so the watcher just sweeps the read-only `~/.claude/file-history` mount and copies anything not yet in `/data/file-history-cache/<session>/`. Polling was the deliberate choice over inotify — filesystem events don't propagate reliably across macOS→Linux bind mounts, and a 60s sweep over ~45MB of stat calls is negligible. Deletions upstream never propagate: once cached, a backup is permanent (that's the point).
- **Serving reads the union.** The file-history endpoints check the live host directory first, then the cache — so from now on, when Claude Code prunes a session's backups, the viewer keeps serving them seamlessly. The response carries an `X-FileHistory-Source: live|cache` header if you ever want to know which copy answered. The availability probe in the Files tab uses the union list too, so cached-only versions stay clickable.
- **Observable**: `curl /api/health` now reports the mirror's last sweep time, total files copied, and cache size — the numbers above came straight from it.

Two honest caveats: backups already pruned before today (the `64ec53fd` case) are gone for good — the mirror can only preserve what still exists from now on; and the cache grows monotonically with the volume (currently 45MB — trivial, but it's unbounded by design since retention is the feature). Memory updated so future sessions know the cache exists and why. Regression suite green.

content.text:
**Verified fixed in real WebKit this time** — no more guessing. The test drives Playwright's actual WebKit engine: wheel over CodeMirror content scrolls the pane 0 → 600, continues over the margin to 1200, and the pane now has real overflow to scroll (scrollHeight 14,963px vs. 539px visible).

The honest post-mortem, because my first two fixes were aimed at the wrong target: the wheel handlers were only an accomplice. The primary bug was that **CodeMirror was clipping its own content** — with default `viewportMargin` it renders only ~a viewport's worth of lines and estimates the rest, which breaks completely in auto-height mode: the editor sized itself to the few rendered lines and `overflow: hidden` swallowed the remainder. Most long previews were silently truncated to ~50 lines with *nothing left to scroll* — in every browser, not just Safari. (My own instrumentation initially "confirmed" the failure against a 7-line `meta.json`, which is what pushed me to look at the geometry instead of the events.)

Three layers now make it correct:

1. **`viewportMargin: Infinity`** — the official auto-height recipe: CM renders every line, so full content exists and the pane has genuine overflow.

3. **Size guard**: content over 512KB skips CodeMirror entirely for a plain `<pre>` (labeled "large content — shown without line numbers"), since fully rendering 40k highlighted lines would take seconds; plain text paints instantly at any size.

Side benefit: previews of long files were truncated *visually* before this — you were never seeing past the first screenful even in Chrome. Reload in Safari; both the scrolling and the full content should now be there.

The self-referential demo is built exactly to your spec — opt-in, in-memory, and clean:

**The seed** (`seed/` in the repo, 3.6MB): this build session's full transcript (1,802 records), its context snapshot, and the transcript of the subagent that redesigned the snapshot tab. Redaction was survey-driven, not guesswork: `demo` (7,048 occurrences) → `demo`, employer and personal project names renamed, and — caught by the verification sweep — your email and name, which my own earlier redaction-survey grep commands had ironically written *into* the transcript as tool inputs. All 35 embedded screenshots are swapped for a 1×1 placeholder since base64 images can't be redacted in place. Every line re-validates as JSON after substitution, and the final sweep confirms zero identifiers across all seed files.

**The mechanism**: `DEMO_SEED=1` loads the seed into a purely in-memory registry at boot — the listing shows it with an amber "demo · the session that built this app (redacted, in-memory)" badge, and every endpoint (transcript, snapshots, companion files, search) serves it from RAM. Nothing is ever written to the data volume, DELETE is refused, and unsetting the variable makes it vanish. Verified end-to-end on an isolated instance: all four API surfaces served the demo with **zero identifier hits**, and its data directory stayed completely empty.

**Your environment is untouched**: the compose default is `DEMO_SEED: "0"`, and the rebuilt live container confirms zero demo sessions in its listing. Someone cloning the repo flips one line in `docker-compose.yml` (documented there and in the README) to explore, in the viewer itself, the session in which the viewer was built — timeline, agent lane, snapshot and all.

One honest note: the demo transcript is a snapshot of this session *as of a few minutes ago* — this very exchange isn't in it. If you ever want to refresh it, the redaction script pattern is in this transcript to re-run against the final session state.

content.text:
Done — Edit and Write tool calls in the preview pane now carry a **"view stored file @vN (nearest by time) →"** button beneath their content, jumping straight to the file-version view for that file: the diff against the previous stored version, or full content for a first version, with the formatted/raw toggle as usual.

How the correlation works, honestly labeled in the button itself: the tool call's absolute `file_path` is suffix-matched against the tracker's cwd-relative paths, and the version chosen is the stored backup whose capture time is nearest the tool call's timestamp — "nearest by time" because rapid successive edits to one file can be a version apart from the exact call you clicked. The link only appears when a stored copy actually exists (live directory or the mirror cache), so you'll never click through to a "backup missing" dead end; edits whose backups were pruned before the mirror existed simply show no link. It works in the JSONL companion-file view's rendered records too, and in agent focus (agent edits are tracked under the parent session's file history, which is what gets queried either way).

Round trip: an edit event → its real on-disk consequence in two clicks, and the file-version view's own listing in the Files tab remains the browsable index of everything that changed. Regression suite green.
